doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

chapter: Harry James, Damone and Los Angeles
title: Road life and leaving Harry James for family
summary: Passing time without phones, his wife's patience, and leaving Harry James after his first child was born.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. This is of course pre-cell phone, pre-walkman, what did you fellas do to pass the time?

Oh well we all had earphones we could put on some kind of music that we wanted to hear. Speaking of that, no cells, no this, no communication at all. It takes a very understanding wife because I couldn’t be in touch with her a lot of the times. We’d be in areas where we were traveling and we didn’t have any access to a phone or time to make a phone call until we checked in someplace. So it took a good woman to put up with us.
I bet they learned what the word gig meant early on.
Did you miss out on some of their things that you wanted to get to or had you settled in one place by that time?

Well I didn’t have the children — after I got out of the service I moved to New York and we didn’t have any children at that point. And then when I moved to Vegas to join Harry James we didn’t have any children yet. And when we had our first child, my daughter, I did about six months with that — and that’s when I told Stan — I mean Harry — I said, “This is too hard, I don’t think I can do this anymore.” However, we used to work 50 weeks a year and we were mostly in Nevada: Reno, Tahoe, Vegas. Reno, Tahoe, Vegas. And we’d go on the road two weeks in the spring, two weeks in the fall. But it got to the point like with the child, packing all the stuff you have to pack and loading the car and then it doesn’t fit and then it snowed in Reno I mean so that’s when I told Harry I said, “I’m going to have to leave. I would love to stay but I need to be home.”
